passages.original: 31. Ὅτι μὲν οὖν καὶ ὑγίεια παρὰ τῆς Ἀρτέμιδος ἀνθρώποις, αὐτὸ μηνύει τοὔνομα, καὶ Αἰνείαν ἴσμεν παρ’ Ὁμήρου μαθόντες ὑπό τε Λητοῦς καὶ ταύτης ἐν μεγάλῳ ἀδύτῳ ῥωννύμενον·
passages.english: 31. That health, too, comes to human beings from Artemis, the name itself makes plain, and we know of Aeneas, having learned it from Homer, that he was restored to strength by Leto and by her in the great inner sanctuary.
passages.notes: "The name itself makes plain" apparently relies on the ancient etymology of Artemis from artemēs, "sound, healthy". The author code xtlg2200 is not identified; the speech appears to be Libanius, Oration 5 (To Artemis).

passages.original: ἀλλ’ αὐτὴ ἐσάωσεν, εἶπεν ἂν Ὅμηρος, καὶ παῖδάς τε γονεῦσιν ἀπέδωκεν ἐμέ τε ἐξείλκυσε σαφῶς τῆς ἐγγὺς οὕτω πληγῆς τῇ περὶ τοῖν ποδοῖν φροντίδι τῷ τε πατρὶ τῷ Διὶ καθαρὸν θανάτων διετήρησε τὸν νεών. εἰ δ’ οὐκ ἐπεκούρει, πόσας ἂν οἰόμεθα δεῦρ’ ἐλθεῖν κλίνας ἀναι- ρησομένας [τότε] τὸ τῆς πόλεως ἄνθος.
passages.english: But she herself saved [them], as Homer would have said: she gave children back to their parents, and she plainly drew me out of so close a blow through the concern for my two feet, and for her father Zeus she kept the temple pure of deaths. If she had not come to our aid, how many biers do we suppose would have come here to carry off the flower of the city [at that time]?
passages.notes: "Through the concern for my two feet" (τῇ περὶ τοῖν ποδοῖν φροντίδι) is obscure. It may mean that she saved the speaker from the blow by making him careful about where he set his feet, or it may refer to some trouble with his feet. The bracketed [τότε] ("at that time") is marked in the edition as doubtful or deleted. ἀναι- ρησομένας is a line-break split for ἀναιρησομένας.

passages.original: ἔξεστιν οὖν μοι φιλοτιμεῖσθαι κατὰ τὸν Σιμωνίδην. ἀδελφοὶ δὲ κἀκεῖνον ἔσωζον Ἀρτέμιδος ὁμοπάτριοι. Σιμωνίδη μὲν οὖν ἀντ’ ᾠδῆς ἐκεῖνα παρὰ τοῖν Διοσκούροιν, ἐμοὶ δὲ ταῦτα καὶ πρὸ Μὴς.
passages.english: So I may take pride as Simonides did. Brothers saved him too, [brothers] of Artemis by the same father. Simonides, then, [received] that [deliverance] from the two Dioscuri in return for a song; but I [received] this even before a song.
passages.notes: The author is Libanius (TLG 2200). Simonides was said to have been saved by the Dioscuri, who called him out of a banquet hall just before it collapsed, in return for praising them in an ode. The Dioscuri and Artemis are all children of Zeus, hence 'by the same father'. The final phrase 'καὶ πρὸ Μὴς' is obscure and probably corrupt. 'Μὴς' may be the moon-god Men (Μήν), or a misreading of some other word, such as a form of μήν or a day/month reference. My rendering 'and before Mes' is tentative. The verbs in the last sentence are elliptical and have been supplied in brackets.
